account: On 6 November 2025 Open Climate Fix (OCF), a not-for-profit, announced that Quartz Solar was live in the National Energy System Operator's (NESO) control room. OCF's AI-powered solar PV forecasting tool combines machine learning, live satellite imagery and weather data. It is fully integrated from day-ahead scheduling to real-time control after starting as a Network Innovation Allowance project (The Energyst, 6 November 2025). The announcement says the tool helps avoid at least £30 million in imbalance costs a year and cuts around 300,000 tonnes of CO2. NESO's Carolina Tortora, Head of AI, Digitalisation and Innovation, is quoted saying it can accurately predict solar generation up to 36 hours in advance. She says it is revolutionizing solar forecasts in the control room. She does not state the £30m figure. pv magazine (7 November 2025) attributes the £30 million (US$39 million) per year saving to Quartz Solar itself. It reports OCF's claim of halving forecasting errors across about 300 grid supply points. OCF's website says the forecast is used daily by NESO. The savings are the maker's estimate, not an operator-reported or audited figure. OCF’s April 24, 2025 case study already described control-room use and the same estimated savings. The November announcement therefore does not establish the first deployment date.

ai_role.statement: The machine-learning forecast is the system in use. But both figures (£30m, 300,000 t CO2) come from Open Climate Fix's announcement reproduced by trade press. NESO's own quoted statement confirms deployment and 36-hour accuracy only. No NESO-authored page or regulator document with a savings figure was found.

OCF's AI-powered solar PV forecasting tool combines machine learning, live satellite imagery and weather data. It is fully integrated from day-ahead scheduling to real-time control after starting as a Network Innovation Allowance project (The Energyst, 6 November 2025). The announcement says the tool helps avoid at least £30 million in imbalance costs a year and cuts around 300,000 tonnes of CO2. NESO's Carolina Tortora, Head of AI, Digitalisation and Innovation, is quoted saying it can accurately predict solar generation up to 36 hours in advance. She says it is revolutionizing solar forecasts in the control room. She does not state the £30m figure. pv magazine (7 November 2025) attributes the £30 million (US$39 million) per year saving to Quartz Solar itself. It reports OCF's claim of halving forecasting errors across about 300 grid supply points. OCF's website says the forecast is used daily by NESO. The savings are the maker's estimate, not an operator-reported or audited figure. OCF’s April 24, 2025 case study already described control-room use and the same estimated savings. The November announcement therefore does not establish the first deployment date.

fields.account: On 6 November 2025 Open Climate Fix (OCF), a not-for-profit, announced that Quartz Solar was live in the National Energy System Operator's (NESO) control room. OCF's AI-powered solar PV forecasting tool combines machine learning, live satellite imagery and weather data. It is fully integrated from day-ahead scheduling to real-time control after starting as a Network Innovation Allowance project (The Energyst, 6 November 2025). The announcement says the tool helps avoid at least £30 million in imbalance costs a year and cuts around 300,000 tonnes of CO2. NESO's Carolina Tortora, Head of AI, Digitalisation and Innovation, is quoted saying it can accurately predict solar generation up to 36 hours in advance. She says it is revolutionizing solar forecasts in the control room. She does not state the £30m figure. pv magazine (7 November 2025) attributes the £30 million (US$39 million) per year saving to Quartz Solar itself. It reports OCF's claim of halving forecasting errors across about 300 grid supply points. OCF's website says the forecast is used daily by NESO. The savings are the maker's estimate, not an operator-reported or audited figure. OCF’s April 24, 2025 case study already described control-room use and the same estimated savings. The November announcement therefore does not establish the first deployment date.

Independent measurement of imbalance-cost changes, which is absent here
produced_by: Satellite imagery, numerical weather data and historical generation data for a national PV fleet
A system operator innovation program (NIA) that funded testing before operational integration
A forecast refresh cycle faster than the operator's existing six-hourly weather updates

purpose: Quartz Solar is built to forecast national and regional solar PV output for grid balancing. Operational use for reserve setting is the intended purpose.

ratings.reason: NESO confirms operational use and 36-hour forecasting. The £30m saving is OCF's estimate, so no measured outcome is documented.
The 300,000-tonne CO2 figure is the maker's estimate. No independent measurement is documented.

summary: Open Climate Fix's machine-learning solar forecast is live in NESO's control room; OCF claims at least £30m a year in avoided imbalance costs, a figure NESO's quoted statement does not give.
system: Quartz Solar (Open Climate Fix machine-learning solar PV forecast, formerly PVNet)
title: Open Climate Fix's Quartz Solar goes live in NESO's control room and may avoid £30m a year in imbalance costs

value.quote: Since adoption, Quartz Solar has halved forecasting errors, according to Open Climate Fix, equivalent to saving at least GBP 30 million in imbalance cost per year, with potential to increase to GBP 150 million ($197.0 million) per year in 2035 if government solar capacity targets are met.
value.who: Great Britain's electricity system operator NESO and, through balancing costs, consumers
